title: Sharing Business Logic
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of sharing business logic using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates sharing business logic.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Sharing Business Logic** as part of **Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform**. Apply sharing business logic by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail. Use the subtopics—Shared Domain Models, Validation and Business Rules, Reusable Data and Network Layers—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Multiplatform work succeeds when shared code depends only on common APIs and platform-specific code is isolated behind deliberate interfaces.

items.title: Shared Domain Models
items.text: Shared Domain Models should support a clear object invariant: make valid states easy to represent, restrict mutation to the intended API, and keep initialization and dependencies explicit.

items.title: Validation and Business Rules
items.text: Validation and Business Rules defines a trust boundary. Validate untrusted input at the boundary, keep secrets server-side, check authorization where the protected operation occurs, and test both allowed and rejected cases.

items.title: Reusable Data and Network Layers
items.text: Reusable Data and Network Layers crosses a system boundary. Model success and failure, validate external data, apply timeout/retry rules deliberately, and keep credentials and database access out of presentation code.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Run inside a Kotlin Multiplatform project with the target toolchains installed; common and platform-specific source sets have different APIs.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Sharing Business Logic removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
